corrections.why: 19.5 m is 64 ft, the height in a 1927 proposal to build a tower on the bluff. The Register gives the standing tower as 80 feet, which is 24.4 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1927 newspaper item proposed a 64-foot tower, the 1940 survey (as the Register quotes it) gives an original 84-foot tower, and the Register gives the standing tower as 80 feet. The standing tower's 80 feet is used.

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page is the only tower-specific source. The Forest Lookouts page supplies the 1927 proposal only. The 1940 survey is cited as the NHLR quotes it; the survey itself was not read. The Register does not say whether the 1939 tower was moved or whether a new tower went up in 1951, so the story keeps both dates and says the sources disagree. The 64-foot height in the brief is a proposal, not a built tower. Agency is supported by the statewide DNR decommissioning statements, not a tower-specific deed. The sources read do not name the current owner or say whether the tower was sold after 2015. Access, climbability and rental are not in any source read, so no access level or visit fact is recorded. No photos added. Not verified: whether the tower has been moved, sold or restored since the 2017 registration. The 39-tower figure in the 2021 chapter report includes towers conveyed to the Menominee Tribe, USFS and the Department of Military Affairs, so the story says landowners, not private landowners.
